title: Deterministic slew & backoff policy for Dedicated fleet autoscaler
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Implement a deterministic slew-rate controller combined with exponential backoff and quantized capacity steps for Redwood Dedicated fleets. This ticket defines the policy engine behavior when converting target metrics (latency & throughput targets) into scaling actions, and the safety limits applied to prevent cascading scale oscillations, cost spikes, or unfair tenant bursts. We want predictable, explainable scaling decisions that respect per-tenant contracts (throughput guarantees) and fleet-level headroom budgets.

Scope:
- Policy synthesis layer that consumes target metrics (p50, p95 tail latency, throughput utilization, sustained qps) and produces a numeric desired capacity delta.
- Slew limiter: deterministic max delta per minute with hysteresis windows to avoid oscillation.
- Backoff: exponential slowdown when scale actions repeatedly fail to achieve target, plus cooldown on rapid downscales.
- Quantized stepper: round desired capacity to allowed instance/pool granularity using capacity buckets (e.g., 1 GPU, 4 GPU, 8 GPU).
- Safety fences: per-tenant cap, fleet spike budget, global emergency throttle that can block growth if external constraints are violated (e.g., infra limits).
- Observability hooks and experimentation flags for canary rollout.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use deterministic slew instead of purely ML-driven headroom to make behavior auditable for SREs and enterprise customers with throughput SLAs.
- Combine PID-like error smoothing on latency with quantile-based throughput targets (p90 usage > 85% triggers growth) to balance latency-centric and throughput-centric workloads.
- Prefer conservative downscale cadence (longer cooldown) to avoid cost churn and user-visible regressions.
- Quantized stepper reduces fragmentation at the infra layer but can cause momentary overshoot; mitigated via staggered instance drain.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Unit tests cover policy translation from metrics to capacity delta for 6 synthetic workload patterns.
2) Integration load tests (kpack) demonstrate <10% SLA misses for target tenants during 3 controlled growth/decay experiments versus baseline autoscaler.
3) No regressions on cost-per-token beyond 7% in steady-state compared to baseline.
4) Observability: dashboard exists showing desired vs actual capacity, slew-limited delta, backoff state, and reason codes for each scale action.
5) Feature flag gating and rollout plan documented in PRD link.

Technical approach:
- Policy Engine: implement as a stateless translator function within scaling controller that takes: recent metric window (60s/5m), target profile, and current headroom credits. Output: desired_capacity_numerical and reason_code.
- Slew Limiter: deterministic limit defined as min(max_scale_step, floor(current_capacity * slew_fraction)). Default slew_fraction 0.12 per 60s for growth, 0.06 for shrink. Hysteresis: require metric breach for 3 consecutive windows to permit growth.
- Backoff State Machine: states {OK, COOLING, SOFT_BACKOFF, HARD_BACKOFF}. Escalate on repeated failures (failed health checks, allocation timeouts). Exponential backoff multiplier starts at 1.5x, capped at 8x.
- Quantized Stepper: map desired_capacity to nearest allowed bucket; if rounding up causes >20% instantaneous overshoot, instead schedule staggered adds with warmup.
- Safety Limits: enforce min and max per-tenant fractional share, fleet-wide budget floor, and emergency stop that prefers model-fallback routing instead of scaling when infra is constrained.

Observability and debug data: reason_code strings (e.g., "SLEW_LIMIT", "QUANTIZE_ROUND_UP", "BACKOFF_HARD", "HEADROOM_EXHAUSTED"). All scale actions emit traces with metric snapshots, target_profile, and pre/post capacity. Expose these in Console as an events stream and per-tenant timeline view.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: internal dogfood on non-production fleets (feature flag on). Run 2 weeks of synthetic ramp tests and compare against baseline.
- Phase 2: limited tenant opt-in (5 customers with Dedicated) under close SRE monitoring.
- Phase 3: gradual percentage-based rollout across fleets with automated rollback if regression thresholds hit.

Links: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/dedicated-autoscale-policy PR design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/AutoscalerDesign GitHub draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2481

Tests & measurement plan:
- Synthetic scenarios: step ramp, sawtooth, jackhammer microbursts, sustained load.
- Metrics to track: p50/p95 latency, queue length, allocation latency, scaling action latency, headroom credits remaining, cost-per-token.
- Chaos tests: simulate failed allocations and ensure backoff behaves as expected.

Security & compliance notes: no customer data is processed by policy engine; all control plane actions logged and tied to audit stream.

Next steps:
- Finalize policy parameters and run parameter sweep in staging.
- Implement feature-flagged controller code + unit tests.
- Prepare dashboards and alerting rules for rollout.
